penance

PEN-unss -- Latin paenitere, 'to regret,' the same root as 'penitent' and 'repent.' · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Penance is a voluntary self-punishment to make up for wrongdoing.

As penance for breaking the window, Leo spent his whole allowance on repairs and mowed the neighbor's lawn all summer.

Example

After snapping at his sister during dinner, a boy quietly does penance by taking over her dish-washing chores for a week -- not because anyone ordered him to, but because he feels he owes it.

That self-imposed act of making up for a wrong is what turns a week of chores into penance. Unlike 'punishment,' which others impose on you, penance is chosen voluntarily out of genuine regret.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

amends: Amends is what you offer to patch things up after a wrong -- a favor, a repaired fence; the idiom is 'make amends.' Penance runs deeper: it is a self-imposed cost, taken on to punish yourself as much as to fix the harm.

reparation: Reparation is the formal repair of damage done -- often money or labor owed after a wrong, even between nations. Penance is personal and voluntary: chosen out of guilt and aimed at the wrongdoer's own conscience, not a bill to settle.

restitution: Restitution is paying back exactly what your wrong cost -- returning what was taken, paying for what you dented or ruined. Penance is aimed inward instead: a chosen hardship that shows real regret, whether or not it repairs the damage itself.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

defiance: open refusal to accept blame or authority

indulgence: treating yourself leniently or pleasurably

Where it sits · how deeply the wrong is paid for — apology → penance → atonement

apology vs. penance: An apology is a much lighter payment for a wrong than penance -- an apology costs only words, while penance means willingly giving up something real to make up for what you did.

atonement vs. penance: Atonement is graver and grander than penance: penance is the concrete act you perform, while atonement is the full moral repair -- the wiping-out of the wrong itself.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — pen

Root — pen: to regret, cause sorrow (from Latin paenitere, 'to cause sorrow,' rooted in poena, 'penalty')

Suffix — -ance

Suffix — -ance: state or act of (Latin -antia)

Put it together

Put it together: Pen ('to regret, cause sorrow' — from Latin paenitere, rooted in poena, 'penalty') + -ance ('state or act of'): Latin paenitentia meant 'regret.' Penance is regret turned into action — the same root that gives us penitent, repent, and penitentiary.

Use the root in a new word: penitentiary

Use the root in a new word: penitentiary: The morning bus passes the penitentiary just after the second stop.

Root Check

Word Choice

Penance began as a religious term -- to 'do penance' for sins -- and keeps that flavor even in everyday use, where it means voluntarily paying for a wrong: 'As penance for forgetting her birthday, he cooked dinner for a month.'
